source.body:
### Bug Description

`Array.pluck()` with more than one field name returns each item's values in the order that item's keys happen to be in, not in the order of the field names passed in. When items in the array have their keys in different orders (common with data merged from different sources), the inner arrays don't line up, so position 0 is sometimes one field and sometimes the other.

This happens because `pluck` (in `packages/workflow/src/extensions/array-extensions.ts` and its mirror in `@n8n/expression-runtime`) loops over `Object.keys(item)` first and over the requested fields second.

### To Reproduce

1. Add a Set or Code node, or open any expression editor.
2. Evaluate:
   `{{ [{ lastName: 'Doe', firstName: 'John' }, { firstName: 'Jane', lastName: 'Roe' }].pluck('firstName', 'lastName') }}`
3. You get `[["Doe","John"],["Jane","Roe"]]`

### Expected behavior

`[["John","Doe"],["Jane","Roe"]]`: each inner array follows the order of the field names passed to `pluck()`.

### Debug Info

Found by reading the code on `master`, and reproduced with a unit test that calls `arrayExtensions.functions.pluck` directly.

### Operating System

Ubuntu Linux

### n8n Version

master (current HEAD)

### Node.js Version

20.19.2

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted
